scan_approval.description: QA5 (step4b-contract-tests-p3a.md §B, 10 §1 L97-113): the one-time scope-level scan approval record, distinct from the adapter-level network opt-in (`approvals[]`).

approvals.description: QA21-27 (step4b-contract-tests-p3a.md §G/§H, 07 §3 L148-168, 10 §12.3): adapter-level network opt-in rows, distinct from `scan_approval`. One row per (scope_id, tool_id); revoke/invalidation updates `status` in place (rows are never deleted, for audit). `status` is intentionally NOT required at the element level: a legacy row (r9-schema-and-earlier, before `status` existed) reads as `active` (10 §12.3 element-level backward compat) rather than failing schema validation.

approval_pending.description: QA21/25-27 (07 §3 L191-205, 10 §12.3): the single in-flight approval write-order's pending intent (a single object, not an array — approval operations are serialized under `.kcs/.lock`). `approved_at`/`approval_method` are intentionally NOT required at the element level: a legacy pending missing them is not a schema error (10 §12.3 element-level backward compat) — it simply never exact-matches for self-heal/CAS purposes and is cleaned up on the next locked mutation.

approvals_initialized.description: QA21/25-27 (07 §3 L176-205): consumed-marker for the one-time 'initial materialize' exception — set true in the same atomic write as the scope's first approval row publish (explicit or materialized), or as a revoke/self-heal-cleanup that actually removed a pending / revoked a row. `true` with `approvals` empty means the exception is already consumed (fail-closed for blanket auto-materialize), not a fresh scope.
